title: Iraq under the Ilkhans and the Turkmen
subtitle: 1258–1534 · A Ruined Province Ruled from Tabriz — the Mongol Peace, the Jalayirid Flicker, Timur's Skulls, the Black and White Sheep, and the Ottoman–Safavid Frontier Fixed on Iraq

categories.label: Power
categories.subtitle: Ilkhanid Iraq governed from Tabriz, the Jalayirids making Baghdad a capital again, Timur's two sacks, the Kara Koyunlu and Ak Koyunlu Turkmen confederations, the Safavid conquest and the forced Shia turn, the Ottoman conquest, and the tribes who were the real power

categories.label: Conflict
categories.subtitle: The Ilkhanate's dissolution and the war of the amirs, Timur's campaigns and the tower of skulls, the Turkmen displacing the Jalayirids, Otlukbeli and the lesson of firearms, the Safavid conquest and the sectarian massacres, and Suleiman's bloodless entry into Baghdad

categories.label: Order
categories.subtitle: A province ruled from elsewhere, the Ilkhanid fiscal reforms and their limits, the endowed shrine administrations that every regime patronised, the tribal order at its widest, the Turkmen confederation as a form of state, and the coming Sunni–Shia frontier

categories.label: Belief
categories.subtitle: The shrine cities and the Shia clerical presence at Hilla then Najaf, Ghazan's conversion and Öljeitü's Shia experiment, the Sufi orders as the popular religion, the Safavid order that became a state, the reduced Jews and Christians, and the millenarians of the marshes

categories.label: Expression
categories.subtitle: Rashid al-Din and the first world history, the Jalayirid school of painting, Persian and Turkic poetry at the Turkmen courts and Fuzuli of Baghdad, the Mirjan complex and the shrine building, and Arabic learning holding in the shrine cities

categories.label: Thought
categories.subtitle: The Maragha observatory and the last great moment of Islamic astronomy, al-Hilli and the systematising of Twelver law and ijtihad, the age of compilation and commentary, and the Sufi metaphysics of the unity of being

categories.label: Economy
categories.subtitle: The Sawad at its recorded nadir, the pastoral and tribal takeover of the farmland, the reduced caravan and transit trade, the pilgrimage economy of the atabat as the mainstay, and the Safavid canal and shrine investment

categories.label: Technology
categories.subtitle: The firearms revolution the Turkmen missed, the Ilkhanid transmission of Chinese techniques, the transverse vault of the Mirjan hall amid a contracting building economy, and the losing fight with the rivers

categories.label: Exchange
categories.subtitle: Iraq as a corner of the Mongol world system, the Timurid marchland connection, the Ak Koyunlu embassies to Venice, the making of the Ottoman–Safavid confessional frontier, and the trans-regional Shia networks pulled toward the shrine cities

categories.label: World
categories.subtitle: The great reversal from the richest land in Islam to one of the poorest, the confessional and tribal fault lines of modern Iraq laid down, the peripheral centuries of being ruled from outside, and the shrine cities as the surviving Iraq

categories.label: Lives
categories.subtitle: Rashid al-Din the vizier and world historian, al-Allama al-Hilli who made a khan a Shia, Sultan Ahmad Jalayir the poet-king, Fuzuli of the shrine cities, and the tribal shaykh who outlasted every dynasty
